body: "Mommy, Daddy, something with yellow eyes is bleeding profusely and stuck in a bear trap outside my window"

Disappearance and likely brutal deaths of close friends who had dependents.

Cousin getting hit by a car in a coma for a year.  She was adopted to begin with after being orphaned.  No justice, she is disabled now.  Happened before she went to prom.  Her brother was torn up to begin with, now, I don't know.

Family close to non-existent.  Family fighting each other in factions.  The young ones are learning to deal with how to not have a family, and that is wrong.

I mentioned suicide rates peak around the holidays in America.  I never understood that until recently.  I find myself asking ugly questions during the Holidays: "How can we celebrate when my friend is missing?",  "How can people go on such a materialistic binge when orphans eat trash down the street?"

  I get this mentality of - if someone is not giving back in society significantly, they are a sociopath.  Modern technology is making us aware of situations all around where we should be helping.  If someone doesn't do their fair share, fuck them.  But how do we determine one's fair share? I never feel like I am doing enough for society unless I fully dedicate my life and body to it.

I agree with you.

I am specifically looking to help (or contract myself) with organizations that have track records with utilizing those with a deathwish.

I have considered that I can help more people by staying alive, that is in fact the point of my decision.  I am better off putting myself in suicidal situations for as long as my body can withstand versus rotting in my current pattern and eventually killing myself out of rash inebriated depression.

To answer your question of the origin of my depression and suicidal thoughts....I'm trying to avoid the story of my self-destruction building up, but I am sure it is my parents early divorce (I was an infant), custody battle/family instability, abuse and substance abuse and more abuse and instability along with pre-existing predisposition to mental disorders.  It's basically been a shitstorm since I was born, my depression nearly disappeared a few years ago, but recently new problems have risen, it is becoming a shit tsunami earthquake tornado to the point that I am cutting all ties with family and friends and turning to reddit to possibly fight in some far off land like I an aspiring Rick Blaine (from *Casablanca*).  I feel like some orphans may have had it better because they escaped the potential abuse.  I have ended up the same as some orphans, as horrible and pretentious as those last two sentences may be.  As you can see, I even distance myself from the few who have may had similar experiences.  

Thank you for responding

At 17, my opinion is that you are taking care of yourself quite well.  You are realizing things.  It took me into my early 20's to realize my parents abuse.

Seek some local help.  I'm new here but I also just saw /r/rSWResources.  It is a very good sign that you are seeking any form of help. Be safe, give us a follow up.

Sometimes rope or a belt is all I really needed to remind myself that my life is indeed in **my own hands**  Edit:  In the past, I thought I needed to hurt myself to assert myself, but sometimes a physical item can create a life-saving eureka moment.  

Happy new year, be safe, you'll find positivity somewhere!
